mission.title: Editing, Revision and Precision at C2 Level

theory.title: Editing, Revision and Precision at C2 Level
theory.explanation: This mission develops advanced advanced editing. Effective C2 communication requires writers and speakers to make purpose, audience, evidence and degree of certainty explicit. Analyse the context before choosing a register; distinguish established information from interpretation; organise complex material so that decisions and qualifications remain visible.
theory.tip: Use precise terminology, attribute claims, qualify uncertainty and make the requested action explicit.

patterns.label: Define purpose and audience
patterns.pattern: Identify what the audience needs to know or decide.
examples: State the decision required before presenting supporting detail.

patterns.label: Support and qualify
patterns.pattern: Connect each claim to evidence and state relevant limitations.
examples: The findings suggest a pattern, although the sample is not representative.

patterns.label: Structure for action
patterns.pattern: Use signposting, headings and explicit ownership.
examples: The recommendation is assigned to a named lead for review by an agreed date.

patterns.label: Review for integrity
patterns.pattern: Check terminology, attribution, tone and consistency.
examples: Distinguish verified outcomes from projected benefits.

content.passage:
An analyst submitted a policy note that was accurate but difficult to use. Several paragraphs repeated the same recommendation, while pronouns such as 'this' and 'they' referred to more than one possible antecedent. The document also alternated between two terms for the same funding stream. None of these problems changed the underlying data, but together they weakened the reader's confidence in the argument.

The editor first made structural revisions, moving the recommendation to the opening and grouping evidence under three headings. A line edit then removed repetition, clarified referents and made parallel lists grammatically consistent. Finally, a copy-edit checked terminology, dates and cross-references. The analyst reviewed every substantive change to ensure that concision had not removed a necessary qualification.

The final note was shorter, but the editing process was not simply a matter of cutting words. It distinguished structural revision from sentence-level refinement and factual checking. Precision meant preserving the intended claim while making its scope, evidence and implications easier to follow.
